name: Kerehaklu Estate - Blossom Culture
description: With the estate shrouded in fog on a January morning, Pranoy noticed unseasonal blossoms in one of the blocks. There, he had the idea of collecting jarfuls of these blossoms for a starter culture. The goal was to see what happens when Kerehaklu's own microbiome shapes processing. Aiding a 71-hour anoxic fermentation, the blossom culture interacted with naturally processed cherries to build fruity layers and a distinctive jamminess. To preserve this development, the coffee was dried on raised beds for three weeks. Roasted to a light profile, the result is a unique expression of provenance. The cup opens with the aroma of ripe berries, followed by notes of strawberry, orange blossom, pomegranate, and sun melon. A delicate floral finish rounds off each sip. Recommended Resting Period: 12 days Note: This coffee pack is a special release with limited availability and, therefore, cannot be included in a subscription plan.

name: Cold Brew Favorites
description: Few things feel more at home during summer than a glass of cold brew. And when we're brewing a batch, this pairing is our go-to. The pack includes: - Amaltas Blend Named after the yellow blooms that herald the Indian summer, Amaltas brews bright cups with notes of blueberry, creamy milk chocolate, and subtle fruitiness. It's wonderfully refreshing on its own. Tasting Notes: Blueberry, Milk Chocolaty, Fruity Processing: Washed + Natural Roast Level: Light Cold Brew Blend Bold Dark chocolate, toffee, and roasted hazelnut come together in this rich, full-bodied coffee. Enjoy it black, or add a dash of milk for more indulgent cup. Tasting Notes: Dark Chocolate, Toffee, Roasted Hazelnut Processing: Washed Roast Level: Medium Dark

name: Attikan Estate
description: Attikan Estate’s arabica coffee beans come from the Biligiriranga Hills in Karnataka and make for one of our most popular coffees. Sweet with nutty overtones and balanced acidity, this is the darkest of our standard medium roasts and recommended for espresso lovers. It is a versatile coffee that also works for manual brewing methods such as Moka Pot, South Indian Filter and AeroPress. Located to the south of Mysore, the Biligiriranga Hills, or ‘white hills’ are named after the mist that hangs over the region. At 1650 meters, it is amongst the highest coffee growing regions in India and grows Selection 9, Selection 795, Cauvery and Kent varieties of Arabica, along with Silver Oaks, citrus, and fig trees. Recommended Resting Period: 10 Days

name: 13th Birthday Blend
description: This celebratory blend brings together natural lots from Stanmore, Orchardale, and Riverdale Estates in Yercaud, along with a washed lot from Unakki Estate in Chikmagalur, which forms the base. Its flavour profile takes us back to the Black Forest cakes many of us celebrated birthdays with during our teen years. Opening with the aroma of honey and strawberries, the cup has a medium-high body and a round mouthfeel. You'll notice notes of strawberry, chocolate, cherry, and pear, followed by a lingering finish of chocolate-covered strawberries. This blend brews well across a range of methods, including espresso, AeroPress, French Press, Moka Pot, and Pour Over. Equally enjoyable black or with milk, it lends itself to a wide range of recipes. Recommended Resting Period: 10 Day

name: Howdia Estate
description: One of our roasters' favourites, Howdia Estate returns for Harvest '26. It reminds us of a floral black tea, and is among the most delicate light roasts on our roster. Processed using the washed method, it brews cups with low bitterness, bright acidity, and a well-rounded mouthfeel. From the first whiff, it's florality comes through, giving way to a bright, tea-like sip with notes of coffee blossoms and orange marmalade, and a black tea-like finish. For a clean, nuanced cup, we recommend brewing this coffee black as a pour over or using an AeroPress. Recommended Resting Period: 10 days

name: St. Joseph Estate
description: Meet the first coffee from our newest partner farm, run by a community of Jesuit priests whose stewardship of the land spans generations. A washed coffee roasted medium-dark, it opens with warm brown spice aromatics. Each sip carries a syrupy mouthfeel and reminds of grapefruit, roasted almond, and toffee. Its medium-high body gives the cup a comforting depth, complemented by a chocolatey aftertaste. Our roasters recommend brewing it as an espresso, or using an AeroPress, Moka Pot, or French Press. A versatile brew, it pairs well with milk, and holds its own black. Recommended Resting Period: 11 Days

name: Raxidi Lobo Estate - Anaerobic Natural
description: We've been excited to collaborate with Raxidi Lobo Estate since their debut with us last year. So, when we first tasted a sample of this anaerobic natural lot, we knew it had to be a part of Harvest '26 . To bring it to life, the producers started fermenting some of the season's best cherries. Introducing a specially curated yeast strain to the mix, they let the process go on for 48 hours. Finally, slow drying on raised beds for 21 days locked flavour. Roasted to a medium profile, the result is a cup that carries the sweet nostalgia of drinking mosambi juice in summer. It opens with berries and cherry on the nose, then settles into tart-sweet, bright notes of mosambi, green apple, and plum. The mouthfeel is velvety with a medium body, and the finish is long and tea-like. Our roasters recommend brewing it black, either as a pour over, or using an AeroPress. Recommended Resting Period: 11 Days Note: This coffee pack has limited availability and therefore cannot be included in a subscription plan.

name: Kerehaklu Estate
description: Harvest '26 debuts with a bright, citrusy light roast. A Kerehaklu special, it shows Pranoy and Ajoy's sure hand with washed processing. Ripe red Selection 9 cherries collected by seasoned pickers marked the lot's foundation. The producers then used a starter made from the farm's local microbes to aid fermentation. Monitoring temperature and pH regularly, they finished within 37 hours. Next, the coffee was mechanically washed and dried in the shade for three days. Finally, 12 days of polyhouse drying on raised beds locked its flavour. This controlled, aerobic washed process built complexity while harnessing the bean's inherent character. Roasted to a light profile, the coffee delivers clean cups that open with the aroma of orange blossoms and brown sugar. Notes of orange, black tea, and green grapes follow, wrapped in a juicy mouthfeel. Expect low bitterness, medium-high acidity, and a lingering finish of orange marmalade. Our roasters recommend brewing it black, either as a pour over, or using an AeroPress. Recommended Resting Period: 12 Days Note: This coffee pack is a special release with limited availability and, therefore, cannot be included in a subscription plan.

name: Sandalwood Estate
description: A beloved part of our perennial selection, Sandalwood Estate brews cups with tasting notes of rich dark chocolate, sweet prune and zesty orange marmalade. This washed coffee, with coffee beans of the Sarchimor variety, was grown at a lush coffee estate in Coorg. If you’ve tried our coffees from Attikan and Baarbara Estates, you’ll love the chocolatey flavour profile of this medium-dark roast. This heavy bodied coffee has a smooth, syrupy mouthfeel which can best be enjoyed when brewed as an espresso or using a Moka Pot or French Press. The long, sweet aftertaste of butter biscuits and dried fruit comes through beautifully when you allow the brew to cool down a little. Recommended Resting Period: 11 Days

name: Dhak Blend
description: Our Dhak Blend is an ode to one of our favourite Indian trees with its colorful flame-like flowers that signal the onset of Spring. The coffees used in this blend are naturally processed which means that the coffee beans are dried with the cherry, resulting in complex, fruity and sweet flavours. Roasted dark to bring out flavours of dark chocolate and fruit jam, this blend's heavy cocoa body leaves a smooth lingering aftertaste. Our roasting team recommends the Dhak Blend for espresso-based drinks as well as manual brews such as the Moka Pot and the French Press. Recommended Resting Period: 9 Days

name: Silver Oak Café Blend
description: If our baristas have brewed you an espresso-based drink at any of our coffee shops, you’ll be familiar with this special offering since it’s our signature house blend! A small way of bringing our cafe experience to you, this blend features a combination of ground coffee beans, processed using either the washed or the unwashed method. This versatile medium roast is named after the Silver Oak trees commonly found across coffee plantations in Southern India. It works well in espresso-based drinks as well as in manual brews such as AeroPress, pour over or in cold brews. Recommended Resting Period: 8 Days

name: Amaltas Blend
description: An ode to the vibrant burst of yellow that marks the beginning of Indian summers, this blend is our go-to choice for crafting a refreshing batch of coffee including cold brews. In fact, this was originally called the Cold Brew Blend Light but owing to its diversity (its flavours shine through in a Pour Over or Aeropress), we decided to rename it after one of our favourite neighbourhood trees. A blend of washed and natural processed coffees, we’ve roasted it light to accentuate fruity and refreshing citrus notes. The result? Balanced cups with notes of blueberry and milk chocolate, with each sip concluding with a chocolatey finish. This light and fruity favourite is best enjoyed black. Recommended Resting Period: 16 Days

name: Cold Brew Blend Bold
description: Roasted to a medium-dark profile, this blend is perfect for brewing refreshing, full-bodied glasses of cold brew. Expect low acidity, notes of dark chocolate, toffee, and roasted nuts, and a bittersweet finish. Recommended Resting Period: 11 Days

name: Baarbara Estate
description: Coffee beans from Baarbara Estate, roasted to a medium-dark profile, have a wonderful aroma of sweet caramel and dried apricot. We love this coffee’s intense, chocolatey flavour profile. To taste the syrupy, smooth mouthfeel of this coffee, we recommend brewing it as a pour over, an espresso or using an AeroPress, Moka Pot or a French Press. If you’ve enjoyed our coffees from Attikan Estate and Sandalwood Estate, you’ll appreciate the sweet aftertaste and medium acidity of this heavy-bodied coffee. Recommended Resting Period: 8 Days

name: Monsoon Malabar AA- Hoysala Estate
description: We’re excited to bring back Monsoon Malabar from Hoysala Estate. The unique flavour profile of this coffee develops when winds and humidity from seasonal monsoon rain change the characteristics of the coffee beans . While this process has its accidental roots in colonial India when a shipment to Europe was attacked by the full force of monsoon winds, similar conditions have been recreated in a controlled environment for consistency in every lot produced. When roasted medium-dark, the result is a medium-bodied cup that invites with sweet aromas of butter biscuits, treating you to notes of cocoa nib s and dried fruit, concluding with the aftertaste of dark chocolate. Best enjoyed when brewed as an espresso, in the Moka Pot or the French press, the nutty flavour profile of this coffee makes for a delicious cup, either with milk or black. Recommended Resting Period: 15 Days

name: French Roast
description: Our darkest roasted coffee, the French Roast is a blend best enjoyed black for those who like their coffee bold, like a traditional espresso with bittersweet notes. If you’re looking to add milk and still retain a definite bite, this is a great choice. We recommend brewing this as an Espresso or using manual brewing equipment such as French Press or Moka Pot. Recommended Resting Period: 5 Days

name: Kalledevarapura Estate - Pulp Sun Dried
description: Our all-time favourite pulp sun-dried coffee from Kalledevarapura Estate is back! This year’s harvest boasts a medium body and a sweet mouthfeel, perfect for brewing as an espresso, a pour over, with a Moka Pot or an AeroPress. Each cup reveals rich notes of brown sugar, roasted almond, and raisin. Recommended Resting Period: 11 Days

name: Vienna Roast
description: The second darkest of our roasts, this blend, with coffee beans from Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, has great body, low acidity, and is a favourite choice for coffee drinkers who enjoy a strong cup, with its characteristic bittersweet notes. The Vienna Roast is best enjoyed with milk. Best enjoyed with milk, we recommend brewing this as an espresso or using manual brewing equipment such as Moka Pot, French Press, or South Indian filter. Recommended Resting Period: 9 Days

name: Basankhan Estate
description: Basankhan Estate was our first ever single origin dark roast. Now a beloved part of our perennial selection, it comes from a family-owned farm with a rich history spanning over 100 years. At the estate, coffee grows alongside black pepper, oranges, cardamom, lemons, and bananas. As you take a sip, enjoy the velvety mouthfeel reminiscent of dark chocolate, which enhances the overall richness of this brew. The coffee’s body is heavy and round, creating a luscious and full-bodied experience that envelops your palate. If you’ve liked our dark roasts like Vienna and Dhak, you’ll enjoy this one too! Recommended Resting Period: 7 Days

name: Elkhill Estates
description: Our debut coffee from Elkhill, a group of estates spanning 1500 acres, this anaerobic washed lot comes from their first year of specialty cultivation. It brews balanced cups with layers of fruit and spice, and a subtle hint of nuts. Ripe cherries, harvested at elevations between 457 to 1067 MASL, were fermented for 36 hours. Next, they were washed then slow-dried on raised beds for nearly 18 days to preserve their character. Roasted to a medium profile, the result is a cup that opens with the aroma of brown sugar and roasted almonds. Each sip is reminiscent of orange, brown spice, and roasted hazelnut, and ends in a lingering, orange zest-like finish. Our roasters recommend brewing this coffee as an espresso, a cold brew, or using a Moka Pot. It tastes great black and also works well with milk. Recommended Resting Period: 11 Days

name: Araku - Viishalakshi FPC
description: Every harvest brings the excitement of new partnerships and new coffees. This season, we’re proud to introduce our debut lot from Viishalakshi Farmer Producer Company (FPC) in Araku Valley. Named after the valley’s wide-eyed goddess, the FPC brings together 33 tribal villages around Kusumaguda. This lot comes from seven of those villages, where coffee cultivation is led by women and processed at a communal facility. Rooted in natural farming practices for generations, the farmers use composted fruit and vegetable waste to nourish the soil and neem oil treatments to safeguard against pests. Formed last year, Vishalakshi has helped guide these villages from commercial coffee cultivation towards specialty practices. There is now a growing focus on pruning plants, selective picking, proper storage of beans, and careful processing. Roasted to a medium profile, this honey sun-dried lot brews clean, balanced cups. It opens with brown sugar and melon, giving way to roasted almonds, prunes, and a whisper of brown spice. The body is round and syrupy; the finish is long and zesty. We recommend brewing it as an espresso, or using a French Press or Channi. It tastes great black as well as with milk. Recommended Resting Period: 11 Days Note: This coffee pack has limited availability and therefore cannot be included in a subscription plan.

name: Cold Brew Bags - Light Blend
description: Fruity + Refreshing If you enjoy a fruity flavour profile, this one’s for you. Our Cold Brew Light is a refreshing blend that shines with fruity notes of berry and subtle hints of white chocolate, best consumed black. Each box contains Cold Brew sachets of 50g each.

name: The Mocha Mix
description: This duo brings together two distinct takes on a café mocha in a simple, mix-and-drink form. It includes: - Sea Salt Mocha: A little indulgence to drop into your days, with notes of salted caramel, milk chocolate, and candy. Chilli Cinnamon Mocha: Spicy and bold with deep cocoa notes, balanced by a hit of chilli, and a lush, date-like sweetness.

name: The Sunrise Combo
description: Enjoy starting your day with a comforting, milk-based brew? This pairing brings together two of our favourite recipes in a simple, mix-and-drink form. It includes: - Signature: Reminiscent of the lattes we serve in our cafes, this Drop brews cups with notes of caramel, grapes, and chocolate. Jaggery: This Drop reminds us of a rich cup of South Indian filter coffee, and brews cups with notes of toffee, dark chocolate, and vanilla.

name: Coffee Cascara
description: This delicious cold brew was made using a little known byproduct of coffee processing - Cascara, the dried skin of coffee cherries. With its tea-like flavours, this unique option is perfect for people looking for something fruity and light bodied. All our cold brews use 100% Arabica, are sourced directly from India’s best farms and are roasted with precision for a unique flavour. Ingredients: Filtered water, Arabica coffee cherry Nutritional Values (per 100ml): Energy 9 cal, Carbs 0.9g, Natural Sugar 0.9g, Protein 0.5g, Total Fat 0.4g Each can is 250ml. This product contains no added sugars. You can purchase this as a pack of 2 or 6. Save 12% when you purchase a pack of 6!

name: The Teenage Trail - Box of 13 Coffees
description: This limited-release marks our first teen year, bringing together thirteen of our most-loved brews from across regions, roast levels, and flavour profiles. And if you've been meaning to give your coffee routine a stir, this is a great place to start. You'll revisit cups that you have returned to over the years while finding new favourites along the way. The selection includes 30g tasting jars of: Garigekhan Estate A bright, layered cup showcasing Castillo, a resilient Arabica variety created specifically to combat leaf rust. Roast Level: Light | Processing: Washed| Tasting Notes: Grapefruit, Pomegranate, Cherry Riverdale Estate – Aroma A layered, fruit-forward cup, bright with the aroma of berries and pineapple. Roast Level: Light | Processing: Natural | Tasting Notes: Floral, Candy, Berries Seethargundu Estate A delicate and complex coffee from a Demeter-certified estate that treats their land as a living ecosystem, nurturing soil health, biodiversity, and long-term balance. Roast Level: Light | Processing: Washed | Tasting Notes: Sweet Lime, Black Tea, Stone Fruit Baarbara Estate – Intenso Yeast An experimental lot processed with intenso yeast, a yeast usually used by beer brewers. Roast Level: Medium | Processing: Washed + Natural | Tasting Notes: Cherry, Chocolate, Strawberry, Pear Silver Oak Blend Our signature blend that brings a little of our cafe experience to you. Roast Level: Medium | Processing: Washed + Natural | Tasting Notes: Hazelnut, Honey, Grapes Amruthavarshini Estate A fruity and nutty coffee, sourced from a women-led estate. Roast Level: Medium | Processing: Natural | Tasting Notes: Cherries, Pineapples, Roasted Almonds MSP Orchardale Estate A fruity and punchy coffee from the misty high peaks of Yercaud. Roast Level: Medium | Processing: Natu

name: Everyday Essentials Matcha Kit
description: This beginner-friendly kit presents a fuss-free way to start a matcha routine. Created by our friends at Got Tea, it pairs ceremonial-grade matcha with the two tools that matter most for daily preparation, a bamboo scoop and a matcha whisk. The kit includes: Ceremonial-grade matcha powder (60 g) Chashaku (bamboo scoop) for precise measuring Chasen (matcha whisk) to achieve a smooth, even texture

name: Full Experience Matcha Kit
description: This kit brings together everything you need to prepare matcha the traditional way. Created by our friends at Got Tea, it is designed to help you learn the craft or refine an existing ritual. Inside, you will find ceremonial-grade matcha paired with the essential tools for a balanced, well-textured cup. A clear, step-by-step manual guides you through each stage, helping you understand not just how to prepare matcha, but why each step matters. The kit includes: Ceremonial-grade matcha powder (60 g) Chawan (matcha bowl) for comfortable whisking Chasen (matcha whisk) to achieve a smooth, even texture Naoshi (whisk stand) to help retain the whisk’s shape Chashaku (bamboo scoop) for precise measuring Sieve to remove clumps before whisking

name: Iced latte Cans
description: Creamy, delicious and strong — your favourite iced coffee is now ready to drink at home! Carry a chilled can of our newest Iced Latte anywhere you go. Made from our signature shot of espresso and double-toned milk, it’s sure to become your go-to caffeine fix. How it’s brewed: Milk and sugar are added to barista brewed espresso shots to make this refreshing iced latte. Ingredients: Milk (70%), Coffee (20.5%), Water, Sugar (3%), Acidity regulators (E340, E452, E339(iii)) Nutritional Values (per 100ml): Energy 50.96kcal, Carbs 9.79g, Natural Sugar 3.59g, Added sugar as sucrose 2.96g, Protein 0.61g, Total Fat 1.29g, Cholesterol 0mg, Sodium 12.69mg Each can is 240ml. You can purchase this as a pack of 2 or 6.

name: Mixed Bag | Drop - Specialty Coffee Concentrate
description: Enjoy some of our favourite recipes in a simple mix-and-drink form. This mixed bag contains: - Americano: A dependable daily driver for those who like their coffee black. Signature: Our go-to Drop for milk-based brews with just the rich touch of sweetness. Sea Salt Mocha: A little indulgence to drop into your days. Chilli Cinnamon Mocha: Spicy and bold with deep cocoa notes, balanced by a hit of chilli, and a lush, date-like sweetness. Jaggery: Rich, velvety, and comforting.

name: Jaggery | Drop - Specialty Coffee Concentrate
description: This Drop reminds us of a rich cup of South Indian filter coffee, and is just what we imagine comfort in a cup to be like. With notes of toffee, dark chocolate, and vanilla, it tastes great black, and also pairs well with milk.

name: Chilli Cinnamon Mocha | Drop - Specialty Coffee Concentrate
description: Inspired by one of our most-loved cafe drinks, This Drop balances deep cocoa notes with a hit of chilli and a lush, date-like sweetness. With minimal bitterness, it is perfect for days that call for a little bit of spunk. We love it with ice and milk. But, feel free to make it your own with any twist you like.

name: Sea Salt Mocha Drop | Specialty Coffee Concentrate, Box of 5
description: Specialty coffee, ready to pour. Salted-caramel sweetness, no equipment. Drop is a single-serve liquid coffee concentrate. Tear, pour into 180ml of milk, stir. Hot or cold, your call. Sea Salt Mocha Tasting Notes: caramel, salted milk chocolate, hints of candy. Sweet, balanced by sea salt, never cloying. Made with our specialty arabica. Not instant powder. Not a syrup. Concentrated coffee, dosed for one cup. Box of 5 single-serve packs. Each pack makes one 180ml cup. Pairs well with cold milk over ice, hot milk for a quick cafe-style cup, or poured over vanilla ice cream for a 30-second affogato. Drop is how we make our specialty coffee work for the days you don't have three minutes to brew. Each Drop pack is a single-serve liquid concentrate, made with our specialty arabica. You tear the top off the pack, pour the contents into 180ml of milk — hot or cold, your choice — give it a stir, and drink. The whole thing takes about thirty seconds. Sea Salt Mocha is our indulgence flavour. The base is the same specialty coffee that goes into our other Drops, but we've layered in caramel and salted-milk-chocolate notes, then balanced the sweetness with sea salt so it doesn't tip into syrupy. You taste the chocolate, then the caramel, then a clean salt note at the end. It's the Drop we reach for in the evening rather than the morning. A few practical things. How to use it: pour the contents of one pack into 180ml of milk and stir. If you want it cold, pour over ice with cold milk and you have a salted-caramel iced mocha. If you want it hot, warm your milk first, then add the Drop. Trying it over vanilla ice cream as a 30-second affogato is, in our experience, also a good use. Box of 5 is the right starter. If you already drink Drop and just want a flavour swap from your usual Mixed Bag, this is also where to go. Shelf life: each unopened pack is good for the printed best-before date (typically several months). Once you open one, use it in that sitting; it's a single-serve dos

name: Signature | Drop - Specialty Coffee Concentrate
description: Reminiscent of the lattes we serve in our cafes, this Drop is our go-to base for milk-based brews. It's just sweet enough and brews cups with notes of caramel, grapes, and chocolate. Feel free to make it your own with any twist you like.

name: Americano | Drop - Specialty Coffee Concentrate
description: This Drop brews a solid, satisfying cup of black coffee with notes of cocoa, dried fruits, and toffee. With medium bitterness, it is both a dependable daily driver and a great base for coffee experiments. We love it as is but feel free to make it your own with any twist you like.

name: Riverdale Estate - Gesha Natural
description: A decade ago, Prakashan from Riverdale Estate planted Gesha, one of the world’s rarest coffee varietals, on his farm in Yercaud. In 2023, after eight years of care, came Riverdale’s first Gesha harvest—one that we roasted as part of our debut Nano-X lineup. Since then, this rare varietal has become a core part of our Nano-X, a limited-edition series featuring experimental lots, crafted by a handful of producers and creative Blue Tokai roasters. This year’s produce, as Prakashan puts it, is the best so far. The plants have matured and come into their own. The processing has become more and more refined over harvests. And thanks to Subham’s seasoned hands, the same goes for our roasting. The lot we sourced was processed using the carbonic maceration method. Ripe, high-density cherries were placed in purpose-built drums. Using special valves, the drums were made oxygen-free and CO2 rich. This controlled fermentation pushed the Gesha’s already exceptional character and complexity further. Slow, controlled drying helped lock in these developments. Given the high density of the beans and their delicate aromatics, this Gesha was a worthy challenge for Subham. Drawing on both experience and a bit of experimentation, he added airflow during the development phase of roasting by opening the hopper chute. This reduced the heavy caramelisation that usually builds at this stage, creating an air-roaster-like profile and unlocking striking clarity in the cup. We’re excited to present the result: an exceptional nano lot that opens with the aroma of sun melon and orange blossom. A bright and silky mouthfeel reveals layered notes of canary melon, cherries, jasmine, and wild berries. Finishing each sip is an aftertaste of cranberries, adding yet another layer of delightful complexity to your experience. We recommend this coffee black, brewed as a Pour Over, or using an AeroPress. Recommended Resting Period: 6 Days Note: This coffee pack is a special release with limited availability an

name: Kolli Berri Estate
description: Our first coffee from Harvest ‘24 is a medium-dark roast with chocolatey and nutty flavours. This single-origin ground coffee hails from the beautiful Kolli Berri Estate, set in Chikmagalur, Karnataka. While brewing this one, you’ll notice the unique characteristics of the coffee beans , starting with the aroma of dried fruits, followed by a syrupy mouthfeel in every sip. With medium acidity and medium- high bitterness, it offers a full-bodied profile which is enhanced when brewed as an espresso or using an AeroPress, Moka Pot or a French Press.

name: Amruthavarshini Estate
description: Meet our second release by Amruthavarshini Estate, a women-led estate run by a mother-daughter duo. Processed using the anaerobic natural method, this medium roast brews fruity and nutty cups with a pleasant sweetness. A honey-like aroma leads into bright notes of cherries and pineapples. The nuttiness of roasted almonds adds depth, while the mouthfeel remains syrupy. In the finish, you’ll taste the lingering aftertaste of raisins and nuts. Our roasters recommend brewing it as an espresso, a Pour Over, or using an AeroPress. It tastes great whether you enjoy it black or with milk. Recommended Resting Period: 12 Days

name: Gulnaar Gift Hamper
description: A luxurious pick for new beginnings, this hamper is made for couples who want the full café experience at home. This hamper includes: - A sleek and compact Mage espresso machine (1 unit) - Smooth, oaky dark roast coffee with overtones of cocoa (250 grams, French Press Grind) - Chocolatey and nutty medium dark roast coffee with fruity overtones from Attikan Estate (250 grams,  French Press Grind) - A medium roast coffee blend with fruity overtones (250 grams, French Press Grind)

name: Palasha Gift Set
description: This thoughtfully curated gift set brings together everything you need for great coffee at home. This hamper includes: - A sleek and compact Maven capsule machine (1 unit) - Box of bold, bittersweet, oaky dark roast coffee capsules (Pack of 10) - Box of chocolatey and nutty medium dark roast coffee capsules (Pack of 10)

name: Winter Blend
description: Meet the blend our roasters look forward to crafting each winter. Pairing well with milk, it is also a solid base for all those winter recipes you've been saving. We've created it using a careful mix of natural and washed lots from St. Joseph Estate and Attikan Estate. Opening with the aroma of brown spices, this coffee has a medium body and a syrupy, round mouthfeel. You’ll be able to taste cinnamon, cacao, roasted almonds, and raisins, and tying everything together nicely is a chocolatey aftertaste. We recommend brewing it as an espresso, or with a Moka Pot or French Press. Recommended Resting Period: 10 Days

name: Monsoon Malabar | Medium-Dark Roast - Easy Pour
description: Nutty + Earthy If you like your coffee dark, but not too much, our Monsoon Malabar AA is perfect for you! With earthy notes, this big-bodied coffee finishes nutty with minimal acidity and notes of spice. Choose from our pack of 5 or pack of 10 Easy Pour boxes.

description: Want to try different flavours before deciding which one to settle on? Order our 5-in-1 Explorer pack and find a new favourite! This pack is a curated collection of five different coffees with different flavour profiles from our wide range of Indian coffees: A balanced Silver Oak Blend A bold and bitter Vienna Roast A chocolatey and nutty coffee from Attikan Estate A chocolatey and nutty coffee from Baarbara Estate A balanced Amaltas Blend Each Sampler Pack will contain 75 g x 5 pouches of whole coffee beans or ground coffee .

name: Taanka | Festive Special
description: This handmade cup sweater was created in collaboration with The Kalaa Store. Featuring a reindeer motif, it makes a thoughtful Christmas gift for your loved ones. name: Riverdale Estate – Fruit Punch
description: Producer Series ’25 opens with a welcome return from Prakashan Balaraman of Riverdale, a pioneer pushing boundaries through experiments with fruit fermentation and rare varietals. For this special lot, Prakashan went a step further, using a blend of tropical fruits during fermentation instead of just one. Ripe cherries were handpicked and triple-washed to remove any floaters before fermentation began. During the first stage, tropical fruits were added in just the right amount to prolong fermentation with natural sugars. Next, in purpose-built tanks, CO₂ was used to flush out oxygen, creating a low-oxygen environment that extended fermentation even further and deepened complexity. After slow drying on raised beds, the coffee was allowed to rest for six weeks for the flavours to stabilise. Choosing a light roast profile, our head roaster Shreyas helped shape a cup that opens with the aroma of rich tropical fruits. Bright notes of peach and strawberry follow, layered with hints of red grape and tangerine. A juicy mouthfeel carries through to a clean, lingering mango finish—all coming together to deliver the fruit-forward character that inspired the name, Fruit Punch. We recommend brewing this expressive coffee black, as a Pour Over, or using an AeroPress. Recommended Resting Period: 18 Days Note: This coffee pack is a special release with limited availability and, therefore, cannot be included in subscription.

name: Ratnagiri Estate - YC 01
description: Run by Ashok and Divya Patre, Ratnagiri Estate has been steadily advancing specialty processing through their science-led approach. In recent years, they have added a microbiology lab, bioprocessing unit, and climate-controlled drying chamber to the farm. With this special coffee, we offer a window into the innovative work they are doing. To process this lot, ripe cherries were placed in bio-reactors after floater removal. In a CO₂ rich environment, two strains of yeast developed using the farm’s own organic matter, together with lactic acid bacteria, drove a 76-hour fermentation. Finally, the coffee was slow-dried on raised beds for 29 days to lock in flavour development. Roasted light by Subham from our team, the result is a cup with both floral and fruity layers. A velvety mouthfeel unfolds into notes of jasmine, custard apple, forest honey, and earl grey tea. Concluding each sip is a tea-like finish. We recommend brewing this coffee black, as a Pour Over, or using an AeroPress. Recommended Resting Period: 8 Days Note: This coffee pack is a special release with limited availability and, therefore, cannot be included in a subscription plan.

name: SICC - Excelsa
description: Most experimentation with specialty coffee revolves around Arabica. But, at Mooleh Manay Estate, Komal and Akshay are asking what else deserves exploration. Researching alternative coffee species, the two are not only working on climate-proofing specialty coffee but are also pushing the boundaries of flavour. This special lot, crafted entirely using beans grown on the Excelsa species, is an example of the same. Since Excelsa is a 20-meter-tall tree, pickers used ladders to harvest the fruit. Ripe cherries were then sorted by submerging in water, removing floaters that are usually underripe or defective. The remaining cherries were then fermented for 84 hours, in a CO2 rich environment, alongside a custom culture. Finally, the cherries were dried inside a polyhouse, with continuous raking to ensure even drying. Tyler, head of our roasting department, and Subham, one of our first roasters at Blue Tokai, collaborated to fine-tune this lot's roast profile. The result is an intense cup that opens with the aroma of wild berries, and treats you to notes of cola, black currant, ripe banana, and molasses. And even when paired with milk, this coffee holds its distinctive and punchy profile. We suggest brewing it as an espresso, a Pour Over, or a French Press. Recommended Resting Period: 15 Days Note: This coffee pack is a special release with limited availability and, therefore, cannot be included in a subscription plan.

name: Garigekhan Estate - CAT - 129
description: We’re excited to share our first release from Garigekhan Estate, a special lot in more ways than one. It marks the estate’s foray into a new Arabica varietal, and showcases what close collaboration between roasters and producers can achieve. In 2020, Garigekhan introduced Catimor 129, a low-intervention varietal, to their land. The producers planted 170 plants and have spent the past few years observing how the variety has taken to their terroir. Naturally resistant to coffee leaf rust and coffee berry disease, Catimor 129 holds fascinating possibilities, especially when processed with care. And this year marks the first time it has yielded a specialty-grade crop. Our Head of Sourcing, Asif, worked closely with the producers to refine the lot’s processing. Learning from last year’s trials, when a shorter fermentation left the mucilage only partially broken down, they experimented with a longer, 120-hour anaerobic ferment. The cherries were then slow-dried over 25 days to allow for deeper flavour development. Roasted to a medium profile, the result is a vibrant cup, lush with fruity layers and a standout nutty note. You'll notice the aroma of red grape first. A sweet, syrupy mouthfeel follows soon after, revealing notes of kiwi, papaya, pomegranate, and roasted hazelnut. A soft, berry-like finish lingers on the palate, punctuating each sip. For the best experience, we suggest brewing this limited-edition lot as a Pour Over, or using an AeroPress. name: Warsanlyngdoh Coffee Collective
description: It's always exciting for us to partner with a new farm. With Meghalaya's Warsanlyngdoh Coffee Collective, that excitement runs even deeper. A completely new coffee growing region for us, it speaks of the possibilities that the North East Indian soil holds for specialty production. The collective’s origin goes back a decade, when Daman, a first-generation coffee producer, visited Nongryniang—a remote village in Khasi Hills and home to the nanny who cared for him in his early years. " There, nestled among the misty hills, I came across two old coffee plants growing in someone’s backyard. I later learned that back in the 1980s, the government had briefly launched a coffee planting program in the area. Like many such initiatives, it had long been abandoned and forgotten. But those plants stayed with me. And so did the people .", he recounts. Since then, Daman started a decade-long pursuit of craft and community. From shading systems to post-harvest processing, he spent years learning all it takes to grow high-quality coffee. Over time, the collective has grown in both, resolve and numbers, with 75 farmers now contributing to a harvest. They pick only the ripest cherries by hand, which are sun-dried for 15–22 days depending on weather conditions. The first coffee that we’ve sourced from the collective is a natural lot we’ve chosen to roast to a medium profile. It brews cups that open with the aroma of raisins, unfolding into a creamy mouthfeel. Notes of blueberry, black tea, and khasi mandarin carry through in each sip, with a long, marmalade-like finish. A balanced coffee, it lends well to various brewing methods, including espresso, Moka Pot, French Press, and AeroPress. It is enjoyable on its own as well as in milk-based beverages. Recommended Resting Period: 13 Days

name: Mooleh Manay Estate – CM Natural
description: Returning to our Producer Series after 2023, Komal Sable and Akshay Dashrath share their first experiment with carbonic maceration. Building on the clarity and consistency they achieved with anaerobic fermentation last season, the fifth-generation producers modified their drums to create a CO₂-rich, oxygen-free environment that allows for slower, more controlled fermentation within whole cherries. The process began by removing floaters to select only ripe, dense cherries, followed by a brief pre-drying phase to reduce surface moisture. The cherries were then sealed in drums, and a custom culture was introduced to extend the fermentation. Over 60 hours, this combination of carbonic maceration and yeast inoculation ensured thorough mucilage breakdown and the development of deep complexity. Post-fermentation, the cherries were dried on raised beds inside a polyhouse. Continuous raking over 7 to 10 days ensured even drying until a final moisture level of 11–12% was reached. Roasted light by Rishab from our team, this coffee offers a well-structured cup with notes of fermented red fruit and a bright, juicy sweetness. It opens with the aroma of mixed berries and carries a syrupy mouthfeel, with layered flavours of dried fig, plum, black grape, and mulberry. A chocolatey aftertaste marks the finish, adding further depth. We recommend brewing this expressive coffee black, as a Pour Over, or using an AeroPress. Recommended Resting Period: 16 Days Note: This coffee pack is a special release with limited availability and, therefore, cannot be included in subscription.

name: SKIA Coffee (Pack of 2)
description: This two-pack (100 gms each) brings together distinct coffees from Nelaji Village in Coorg. Grown by smallholder farmers and processed by Ashish Rao, a first-generation producer, these lots mark our first collaboration with Skia Coffee. Ripe, high-density cherries were pulped with the mucilage left intact, then placed in sealed tanks for a 72-hour anaerobic fermentation. A yeast strain purpose-built for controlled fermentation was introduced during this stage to develop complexity. From there, the two lots took separate paths. Honey Sun Dried The first lot was dried slowly on raised beds under controlled shade. Roasted to a medium profile, it makes for a balanced cup with notes of sweet lime, prunes, and almond. Recommended Resting Period: 16 Days Thermal Shock This second lot was immersed in hot water, then rapidly cooled in ice. It was then mechanically washed and dried slowly under shade. Also roasted to a medium profile, it brews cups with notes of tangerine, brown sugar, and berries. Both coffees brew beautifully as an espresso or with an AeroPress, Moka Pot, or French Press. They taste great black and pair well with milk. Together, they offer a chance to explore how thoughtful shifts in processing shape flavour in the final cup. Recommended Resting Period: 12 Days Note: This coffee pack is a special release with limited availability and, therefore, cannot be included in subscription.

name: Kerehaklu Estate - Peaberries
description: This special two-pack( 125 gms each) , crafted in partnership with Kerehaklu Estate, features our favourite mutation, a Peaberry. Coffee cherries usually hold two seeds but about 5-10% of the time, just one seed grows inside the cherry. This is a Peaberry. Small, round, and denser than regular coffee beans, it boasts a unique flavour profile, with a deeper sweetness and a brighter acidity. Carefully isolated by Pranoy, Ajoy, and team at the farm, the Peaberries that lent to the creation of this pack were processed in two distinct ways: - Washed (Aerobic Sequential) This lot underwent a sequential aerobic fermentation, where Peaberries were submerged in water for an extended period, creating an oxygen-rich environment that brought out complexity, clarity, and bright acidity. Roasted light, these make for a cup with the aroma of brown sugar and citrus, and a juicy mouthfeel that opens into notes of mosambi, toffee, and green grape. The aftertaste is sweet and reminds of ripe mosambis. Natural (Anoxic) Fermented in an oxygen-free environment, the coffee cherries in this lot experienced a slower, more complex fermentation, since the microbes had more time to break down the sugars present, and produce a wider range of aromatic compounds. The result is a rich, fruity flavour profile with a deep body and balance. Roasted light, these make for a cup with the aroma of red grape and dark cherries, and a creamy mouthfeel revealing notes of orange, red grape, and red apple. Punctuating each sip is a lingering aftertaste of red apple. We recommend brewing these coffees black as a Pour Over or using an AeroPress. Recommended Resting Period: 15 Days Note: This coffee pack is a special release with limited availability and, therefore, cannot be included in our Mixed Bag subscription.

name: MSP Micro Lot Blend
description: A melting pot of micro-climates where some of India’s finest coffee has thrived since 1920, MSP Coffee is a group of seven estates in Yercaud, including the three that lend to this blend. From achieving a surprisingly sweet cup after fermenting coffee with a local variety of bitter lemons to seeing the tail end of a 1000-hour ferment, the group exemplifies how curiosity lies at the heart of their work. The micro lots we picked for this blend come from Bison Valley Estate, Stanmore Estate, and Orchardale Estate and bear this very spirit. The first lot was washed and fermented with melon extract, with the processing imparting a unique sweetness. The second underwent triple fermentation: first as whole cherries, then after depulping, and finally after washing. This process uniquely combined quick dry fermentation and long anaerobic fermentation with watermelon, developing complexity. The third coffee was processed using the natural method, with cherries dried intact, allowing the fruit to shape its character. Roasted medium, the blend has a fruity and punchy flavour profile with notes of cherry, dark chocolate, and wild berry, followed by a rich, lingering aftertaste of chocolate. This blend works well black as well as with milk and lends itself nicely to most brewing methods including espresso, Pour Over, Moka Pot, French Press, AeroPress, and Cold Brew. Recommended Resting Period: 7 Days

For the third destination, we bring you three 75g packs of coffee from Yercaud, a picturesque hill station dotted with streams and valleys, where coffee has been cultivated since 1820. name: Riverdale Estate - White Rose
description: Fermented with rose petals, this layered light roast perfectly embodies why Riverdale Estate is a pioneer in experimental processing. Only the ripest cherries, hand-picked from the higher-altitude blocks of the farm, where the fruit matures slowly and develops an enhanced sweetness, were used. Once harvested, the cherries underwent a triple wash with natural spring water to remove impurities, followed by a floating process to eliminate underdeveloped beans. During fermentation, rose petals were introduced, setting up the stage for complexity in the cup. After fermentation, the cherries were slow-dried on raised beds for up to 30 days, allowing for even drying. Finally, the coffee was hulled at the estate’s dry mill, where any defective beans were eliminated before being sent to our roastery. In the cup, you’ll experience bright notes of blood orange, passion fruit, and pomegranate, complemented by a creamy mouthfeel and a lingering sweetness. We recommend brewing it black using an AeroPress or as a Pour Over. Note: This coffee is a special release with limited availability and, therefore, cannot be included in our Mixed Bag subscription.
